feedback:
Written before this candidate races, so it states no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 3 (score 396.3, the best so far): oval finish 1.0 at 1.7 s with max_error 0.016 and zero line-loss events, but s-bend progress 0.46 with max_error 0.064 and 1.25 line-loss events, and slalom progress 0.09. Iteration 2 changed sensor size, span, wheel track, speed and kp together, and the oval fell to 0.45, so its s-bend result cannot be attributed to the span. Iterations 4 and 5 show that speed, gain and turn-rate changes cost oval completion, so this candidate is right to leave them alone. It changes only the outer sensor span (x = ±0.03 to ±0.04) and keeps the 12 mm footprint, mass, wheel track, speed and gains from iteration 3. That isolates the span effect for the first time. The contract is satisfied and the candidate is valid. Approve it: it is the cleanest test available from the best design, and the race will show whether the span limits bend survival.

Watch item: at 2 cm spacing with 12 mm footprints, there are 8 mm gaps between adjacent sensors. The 25 mm tape should still be seen by at least one sensor near centre, but check line_loss_events on the oval first. If the oval loses completion or line_loss_events rise there, the gaps are the cause, and the fix is an intermediate span (about ±0.035) or a 16 mm footprint, not a larger gain change.

After the race, read the results in this order. (a) If s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1 and s-bend progress rises above 0.5 while the oval still completes at 1.0, keep the wider span and try ±0.05 at the outer sensors next. (b) If oval completion holds but s-bend progress is flat, the span is not the limit, so return to the iteration 3 layout and test wheel_track 0.09 alone. (c) If oval completion falls or steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3, revert to ±0.03 before changing any gains.
requested_changes: If s-bend line_loss_events fall below 1 and progress rises above 0.5 with oval completion still 1.0: keep sensor x at ±0.04 and try ±0.05 for the outer sensors, since iteration 3 showed the 0.06 m limit is reached just after the line leaves the ±0.03 array.

If oval completion drops below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.3: revert the outer sensors to ±0.03 and keep the other fields, because the 8 mm gaps at 2 cm spacing may be dropping the signal on the oval.
If s-bend progress does not move: keep the wider span and test wheel_track 0.09 alone, because iterations 1 to 3 showed narrower track raised bend progress without losing the oval.
